message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"20.1","text":"During the night, he rose, woke us, and sat down as usual. He said, “Ask me about whatever you wish.” Sophonias was the first to begin with him: “Since we desire to learn, explain to us how the account concerning the evil one truly stands.” Peter said, “I have indeed already made it clear through the discussion with Simon, but because the things concerning him were stated together with other points, the matter was not brought to light very clearly. For many points that seem equal in force to the truth give most people some knowledge of the truth itself. Therefore, if I now tell you what I had then told Simon among many points, do not suppose that you have been honored equally with him.” Sophonias said, “You speak rightly. For if you now separate it out for us from the many points stated then, you will make the actual truth clearer.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"πονηροῦ","chosen":"the evil one","rationale":"The adjective is substantival and contextually denotes the personal evil ruler discussed in the following sections; “evil” as an abstraction is a possible broader alternative."},{"source_quote":"κεφαλαίοις","chosen":"points","rationale":"The word denotes principal points, headings, or topics in an argument."},{"source_quote":"αὐτῷ","chosen":"with him","rationale":"In the warning about equal honor, the pronoun most naturally refers to Simon. A reference to the subject matter is less consistent with Sophonias’s reply."},{"source_quote":"ἀφορίζεις","chosen":"separate it out","rationale":"The verb means to distinguish or set apart; its unstated object is contextually the matter under discussion."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"20.2","text":"Peter said, “Hear, therefore, the truth about the ordering concerning the evil one. God defined two kingdoms and constituted two ages. He decided that the present world was to be given to the evil one because it is small and passes away quickly, but he promised to give the coming age to the good one, since it is great and eternal. He therefore made the human being self-determining, with the capacity to incline toward whatever actions he wishes. His body is three-part and has its origin from the female, for it has desire, anger, grief, and the things that follow these. The spirit—though itself not third in origin but three-part—has its origin from the male and is receptive to reasoning, knowledge, fear, and the things that follow these. Each of the two triads has one root, so that the human being is from two compounds, female and male. For this reason two ways were also set before him, that of law and that of lawlessness. Two kingdoms were also defined: one called the kingdom of the heavens, and the other the kingdom of those now reigning upon the earth. Moreover, two kings were appointed. One is appointed by law to reign over the present and temporary world, and he was blended so as to delight in the destruction of the wicked. The other, himself also being king of the age that is to come, loves the whole human race. Unable in the present circumstances to have freedom to speak openly ..... as, while trying to conceal who he is, he counsels what is beneficial.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ἁρμονίας","chosen":"ordering","rationale":"The noun can denote an arrangement, composition, or harmonious ordering. “Ordering” suits the ensuing account of paired ages, kingdoms, rulers, and elemental mixtures."},{"source_quote":"αὐτεξούσιον","chosen":"self-determining","rationale":"The term describes possessing authority over one’s own choices, not unlimited power."},{"source_quote":"τριτογενὲς","chosen":"third in origin","rationale":"The contrast distinguishes being third-generated or third in derivation from being three-part. “Third-born” is a more literal alternative."},{"source_quote":"φυραμάτων","chosen":"compounds","rationale":"The word evokes kneaded masses or mixtures and supports the author’s composite anthropology."},{"source_quote":"χειροτονεῖται","chosen":"is appointed","rationale":"The verb denotes selection or appointment; the accompanying reference to law presents the rule as authorized."},{"source_quote":"ἐκράθη","chosen":"was blended","rationale":"The compositional force is retained because the following section explains the rulers through elemental blending."},{"source_quote":"παρρησίαν","chosen":"freedom to speak openly","rationale":"The noun can mean boldness, freedom of speech, or openness. The following effort to remain concealed favors open speech or action."},{"source_quote":"λανθάνειν","chosen":"to conceal","rationale":"The infinitive describes escaping notice. Here it is understood as concealing the king’s identity; “to remain unnoticed” is also possible."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"δυνάμενος .....","issue":"The selected edition prints a lacuna of exactly five dots after this word. Its content is unavailable, no restoration has been supplied, and all five dots are retained in the English.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"ὧς","issue":"The circumflexed form is difficult in this construction and may be an accentual error for the conjunction ὡς. The translation adopts that contextually defensible comparison while disclosing the proposed correction.","proposed_reading":"ὡς","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"20.3","text":"“Of these two ..... compels the other, at God’s command. Each person has authority ........... by which to obey whichever of them he wishes, for the purpose of doing good or evil. If someone chooses to do good things, he becomes the possession of the good king who is to come. But if someone should do base things, he becomes an instrument of the present evil one. Through sin, the latter has received authority over him by a just judgment; and, wishing to do so even before the coming age, he delights in punishing him in the present life and, as one gratifying his own desire, carries out God’s will. The other was created to delight in exercising authority over righteous people. When he finds a righteous person, he rejoices greatly, saving him by eternal life; and he too, as one gratifying himself, offers God thanks for them. Every unjust person may be saved after regretting his course, and every righteous man may incur punishment for a final sin. But these two rulers are God’s swift hands, desiring to act beforehand in accomplishing his will. That this is so is also stated in the law in the person of God: ‘I will kill and make alive; I will strike, and I too will heal.’ For he truly kills and gives life. He kills through the left hand, that is, through the evil one who was blended so as to delight in the affliction of the impious. But he saves and benefits through the right hand, that is, through the good one who was created to delight in benefiting and saving the righteous. These have their substances not from outside God, for there is no other first principle. Yet they were not brought forth by God as living beings, for then they would have shared his disposition. Nor did they arise accidentally, having come into being spontaneously contrary to his purpose, since then the greatest part of his power would have been abolished. Rather, the four primary elements were brought forth from God: hot and cold, wet and dry. Thus he is indeed the father of every substance ..... disposition being what comes after the blending; for when they were blended outside, choice was born as their offspring. At the end of the present world, therefore, the evil one, after serving God blamelessly, can, since he is not of a single substance, become good when recomposed away from persistence in evil. For even now he does nothing evil, although he is evil, since he has lawfully received authority to inflict suffering.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ὥ","chosen":"by which","rationale":"The form is taken as a dative relative whose antecedent may have stood in the preceding lacuna. An erroneous or incomplete construction is also possible."},{"source_quote":"κτῆμα","chosen":"possession","rationale":"The word denotes something acquired or owned and presents the person as belonging to the coming good king."},{"source_quote":"ὑπηρέτημα","chosen":"instrument","rationale":"The formation denotes something that serves or ministers. “Servant” is possible, but “instrument” preserves its contrast with “possession.”"},{"source_quote":"καὶ ὡς ἰδίᾳ χαριζόμενος ἐπιθυμίᾳ","chosen":"and, as one gratifying his own desire","rationale":"The construction with ὡς presents the action under the description of gratifying his own desire while he fulfills God’s will. “As though gratifying his own desire” is also possible, but need not imply that the gratification is unreal."},{"source_quote":"καὶ αὐτὸς δὲ ὡς ἑαυτῷ χαριζόμενος","chosen":"and he too, as one gratifying himself","rationale":"This parallel ὡς construction characterizes the good ruler’s action as self-gratification. The alternative “as though gratifying himself” is possible but does not necessarily deny actual gratification."},{"source_quote":"μεταμεληθέντι","chosen":"after regretting his course","rationale":"The verb can denote regret, reconsideration, or a change of mind. The context entails departure from injustice, but the distinct Greek terminology is preserved rather than homogenized."},{"source_quote":"τελευταίας","chosen":"final","rationale":"The adjective may describe one last sin or a sin committed at the end of life; the rendering leaves both temporal nuances possible."},{"source_quote":"χεῖρές","chosen":"hands","rationale":"The author’s bodily image for the two rulers is preserved rather than reduced to “agents.”"},{"source_quote":"προλαμβάνειν","chosen":"to act beforehand","rationale":"The verb conveys anticipation or acting in advance; the rulers perform divine punishment or benefit before final judgment."},{"source_quote":"οὐ μὴν ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ ὡς ζῷα προεβλήθησαν (ὁμόδοξοι γὰρ αὐτῷ ἦσαν)","chosen":"Yet they were not brought forth by God as living beings, for then they would have shared his disposition.","rationale":"The main text takes the parenthetical imperfect indicative as the consequence implied by the preceding denial: if they had been brought forth as living beings, they would have shared God’s disposition. Greek supplies neither ἄν nor an explicit conditional protasis, however, so a direct indicative assertion remains possible: “for they were of the same mind as him.”"},{"source_quote":"ἔξω","chosen":"outside","rationale":"The adverb is retained without an invented object. It may mean outside God or externally to the original divine bringing-forth."},{"source_quote":"μετασυγκριθεὶς","chosen":"when recomposed away from","rationale":"The participle denotes recomposition or alteration by mixture. The following genitive is taken as separation from persistence in evil; alternatively, that genitive may characterize a hypothetical single substance fixed in evil."},{"source_quote":"κακουχεῖν","chosen":"to inflict suffering","rationale":"The verb describes subjecting others to hardship or maltreatment; the author presents that activity as lawfully authorized punishment."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"τούτων .....","issue":"The selected edition prints a lacuna of exactly five dots after this word, where the grammatical subject or other governing wording may have stood. No subject has been restored, and all five dots remain explicit in the English.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"ἔχει...........","issue":"The selected edition prints a lacuna of exactly eleven dots after this word. The following relative form may depend on an antecedent in the lost wording, but no missing content has been supplied, and all eleven dots are retained in the English.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"οὐσίας .....","issue":"The selected edition prints a lacuna of exactly five dots after this word, between the statement about God as father of every substance and the phrase about disposition. No connective or missing claim has been supplied, and all five dots remain explicit.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"20.4","text":"After Peter said these things, Micaiah, who was also one of the followers, asked, “From where, then, does human sinning come?” Peter said, “It comes from not knowing that, when judgment has taken place concerning the things they do wrongly, they are certain to be punished. Consequently, although they possess desire for the continuation of life—as I said on another occasion—they satisfy it indiscriminately, through the corruption of half-mature boys or through some other pandering sin. Because they do not know that they are judged, as I said before, their lack of fear drives them to satisfy desire unlawfully. Thus God is not evil, for he established desire well so that there might be continuation of life. Rather, they themselves are most impious, since they have used what is good in desire badly. The same reasoning may also be applied to anger: someone who uses it justly, as is permitted, acts piously, but one who goes beyond the proper measure and takes judgment upon himself acts impiously.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ἁμαρτάνειν","chosen":"human sinning","rationale":"The infinitive denotes committing wrong or sin; the question asks for its source."},{"source_quote":"διαδοχὴν","chosen":"continuation","rationale":"The term refers to succession or perpetuation, here the continuation of human life through generation."},{"source_quote":"πληροφοροῦσιν","chosen":"they satisfy it","rationale":"Here the verb describes bringing desire to fulfillment rather than intellectual assurance."},{"source_quote":"ἤμ[ιπεπείρων]","chosen":"half-mature","rationale":"The editorially marked adjective portrays the boys as only partly mature, literally half-ripened."},{"source_quote":"κολακευούσῃ","chosen":"pandering","rationale":"The participle portrays the sin as flattering or catering to desire; “enticing” is another possible rendering."},{"source_quote":"καλῷ","chosen":"what is good","rationale":"The wording distinguishes desire’s good divinely assigned function from its wrongful human use."},{"source_quote":"ἑαυτῷ τὴν κρίσιν λαβὼν","chosen":"takes judgment upon himself","rationale":"The phrase may mean that the person takes judgment into his own hands by assuming authority to judge or punish, which fits the discussion of exceeding the proper use of anger. It may instead mean that he incurs or receives judgment for himself, which fits the preceding emphasis on being judged and punished. The English intentionally leaves both readings available."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"[σεως γε]","issue":"These letters are printed in square brackets within the expression about judgment. The translation follows the resulting selected-edition reading while disclosing its editorially marked status.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"[πον]","issue":"These letters are printed in square brackets to complete the verb translated “I said.” The translation follows that marked reading.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"[εἰς]","issue":"The preposition is printed in square brackets. The translation follows the selected edition’s marked construction without claiming recovery of independently verified wording.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"[ιπεπείρων]","issue":"Most of the adjective is printed in square brackets, and the resulting full printed form is unusual beside the expected form ἡμιπεπείρων. The contextual meaning “half-mature” is defensible, but the marked letters remain editorially uncertain.","proposed_reading":"ἡμιπεπείρων","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"20.5","text":"Sophonias spoke again: “Your patience, my lord Peter, grants us boldness to ask you questions on many points for the sake of precision. Therefore, taking courage, we conduct the examination in every way. I remember, then, that yesterday, while Simon was engaged in inquiry with you, he said that if the evil one was generated from God, it follows that he shares the same substance as the one who brought him forth and ought to have been good, not evil. You answered that this does not necessarily follow, since many evil people are born from good people. In the same way, two individuals unlike each other were born from Adam, one of whom was evil and the other good. When Simon objected that you had used human examples, you answered that by this reasoning one should not accept that God begets either, for this too is a human example. But I, Sophonias, accept that God begets; I do not accept that he begets evil, even if good people among human beings beget evil ones. And do not suppose that I irrationally ascribe to God some things pertaining to human beings but not others, because I concede begetting to him but do not ascribe to him the begetting of what is unlike him. Human beings naturally beget sons whose dispositions are unlike their own for the following reason: because they are composed of four parts, their bodies change in different ways according to different alterations; and in a human body, as the distinctive quality of the alteration at each particular time increases or decreases, it disrupts the proportionate mixture. Because the compounds do not always remain the same, the seeds are secreted at different times with different mixtures, and dispositions, whether good or evil, follow them in accordance with the mixture at that time. But in God’s case no such thing can be conceived, for since he is unchangeable and always existent, wh...... he might wish to bring forth, it is altogether necessary that what is brought forth by him should likewise ...... in every respect in relation to the one who begot it—I mean both substance and disposition. But if anyone should wish to call even him changeable, I do not know how he can also call him immortal.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"μακροθυμία","chosen":"patience","rationale":"The noun denotes forbearance or patience, here Peter’s willingness to endure extensive questioning."},{"source_quote":"παρρησίαν","chosen":"boldness","rationale":"Here the noun denotes confidence or freedom to question Peter openly."},{"source_quote":"ἀκολούθως","chosen":"it follows","rationale":"The adverb marks Simon’s inference that what comes from God must share God’s substance and goodness."},{"source_quote":"προβαλόντι","chosen":"the one who brought him forth","rationale":"The participle describes derivation or production without requiring the more technical English term “emanated.”"},{"source_quote":"ἀνόμοιοί","chosen":"unlike each other","rationale":"The contrast between the evil and good sons favors mutual dissimilarity, though the phrase could instead mean that both differed from Adam in some respect."},{"source_quote":"διαφερόντων","chosen":"pertaining to","rationale":"In context the participle concerns features found among or associated with human beings. “Things in which human beings differ” is grammatically possible but fits the argument less well."},{"source_quote":"τροπὰς","chosen":"alterations","rationale":"The term denotes changes or turnings, possibly including seasonal or elemental variations."},{"source_quote":"ἴδιον","chosen":"distinctive quality","rationale":"The phrase denotes the quality or component proper to a particular bodily alteration, likely one of the elemental qualities."},{"source_quote":"ἀποκρίνονται","chosen":"are secreted","rationale":"The verb has the physiological sense of being separated or secreted in the discussion of bodily seed."},{"source_quote":"ἄτρεπτον","chosen":"unchangeable","rationale":"The adjective directly contrasts God with the changing bodily mixtures described immediately beforehand."},{"source_quote":"γνώμην","chosen":"disposition","rationale":"Here the noun denotes disposition, purpose, or cast of mind. “Opinion” is possible but too narrow for the contrast between good and evil offspring."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"ὅπ......","issue":"The selected edition preserves only the fragment ὅπ before a lacuna of exactly six dots. The English represents the incomplete fragment as “wh......” and does not complete it as “whatever,” “whenever,” or another conjecture.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"ὡσαύτως ......","issue":"The selected edition prints a lacuna of exactly six dots after this word, where wording governing the comparison with the begetter is unavailable. The English retains all six dots and does not supply a verb such as “resemble.”","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"[δὲ θελήσ]","issue":"These letters are printed in square brackets, completing the conditional expression. The translation follows that marked reading without proposing additional text.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]}]}
